decisions.reason: As a renamed version of an already well-accepted trommel screen, it likely performs above aspiration and a mature German machinery firm would have little reason to withdraw it.
The dedicated page, multi-model line, and fit with mobile waste-processing needs suggest sufficient commitment and no clear shortfall that would trigger dropping it.

This grinder line had weaker visible support and possible overlap with related products, so if results disappointed it would face review, but absent evidence of failure the firm would still more likely retain it.

The stationary electric fine shredder is somewhat niche, yet it matches the firm's move toward tougher and more resource-saving stationary solutions, so management would likely keep it unless performance clearly lagged aspirations.

The green-waste grinder appears the most vulnerable because of portfolio overlap and narrower application, but with organizational slack and no explicit sign of underperformance the firm would still more likely continue than exit.
The single-shaft pre-shredder line has strong capability fit, several models, and a clear place in stationary processing, making continuation the more probable choice.
